Topics · Death and what comes after

If karma loses no deed, who keeps the record?

The Quran agrees nothing is lost, down to an atom, asks who keeps the record, and says the keeper is generous.

Part 1 of 3

﴿فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُۥ٧ وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُۥ٨﴾

Translation of the meaning

So whoever does an atom's weight[1965] of good will see it, And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.

Translator's notes

[1965] Or "the weight of a small ant."

Quran · Az-Zalzalah 99:7-8

Translation

For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it is good, or whether it is evil.

Original · Hebrew

כִּ֤י אֶת־כָּל־מַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים יָבִ֥א בְמִשְׁפָּ֖ט עַ֣ל כָּל־נֶעְלָ֑ם אִם־ט֖וֹב וְאִם־רָֽע׃

Ecclesiastes · 12:14

World English Bible

Karma says no act is lost. This verse says the same of the smallest act: whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of harm will see that. On the principle, the Quran is with you. The open question is this: if every act down to the smallest is kept, is anything keeping it? A law of nature needs no keeper. A record does, and an exact record needs a keeper who misses nothing.

A question for you

When you picture the account of deeds being kept, what do you picture keeping it?

If you sayThe act carries its own result, so no keeper is needed
ThenA coherent picture, and centuries old. One question for it: how can a result be exact to an atom's weight, in every mind, without anything knowing the act?
If you sayThe law of the universe, working by itself
ThenClose to what many schools say. The next verse speaks of justice and of a keeper.
If you saySomething that knows
ThenThen the question becomes what such a keeper is like, and the next verse answers that in part.
If you sayI have never needed to picture it
ThenThat is honest. The pull here is curiosity, not duty: when everything is counted, who counts?

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَنَضَعُ ٱلْمَوَٰزِينَ ٱلْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْـًٔا ۖ وَإِن كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَـٰسِبِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We place the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be treated unjustly at all. And if there is [even] the weight of a mustard seed,[887] We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accountant.

Translator's notes

[887] i.e., anything as small or insignificant as a mustard seed.

Quran · Al-Anbiya 21:47

Translation

(let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know my integrity);

Original · Hebrew

יִשְׁקְלֵ֥נִי בְמֹאזְנֵי־צֶ֑דֶק וְיֵדַ֥ע אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ תֻּמָּתִֽי׃

Job · 31:6

World English Bible

The verse adds three things to the principle. First, the weighing is just: no soul is wronged in the least. Second, nothing is too small to be counted: even a mustard seed is brought forward. Third, the account has an accountant: it is enough that the One keeps the reckoning. So the answer to “who keeps it?” is the Quran's usual one: where there is counting, there is one who knows.

A question for you

In any account, which matters most to you: that it be exact, that it be fair, or that it be known to someone?

If you sayExact
ThenExactness is what both verses promise, down to a mustard seed. The question that remains: who holds that exactness across every mind?
If you sayFair
ThenThe verse says no soul is wronged in the least. Fairness needs one who weighs and does not lean.
If you sayKnown to someone
ThenThe verse says it is enough that the Reckoner counts. Whoever wants the hidden good to be known finds the answer here.

Part 3 of 3

﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَظْلِمُ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ ۖ وَإِن تَكُ حَسَنَةً يُضَـٰعِفْهَا وَيُؤْتِ مِن لَّدُنْهُ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, Allāh does not do injustice, [even] as much as an atom's weight; while if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:40

Translation

Who has prescribed his way for him? Or who can say, ‘You have committed unrighteousness’?

Original · Hebrew

מִֽי־פָקַ֣ד עָלָ֣יו דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּמִֽי־אָ֝מַ֗ר פָּעַ֥לְתָּ עַוְלָֽה׃

Job · 36:23

World English Bible

This verse says the one who keeps the account wrongs not even an atom's weight, and that a good deed is multiplied and a great reward is added from His own giving. So the Quran pictures the account kept by one who is exact and generous both.

A question for you

If the account were kept by one both exact and generous, what would change in what you do today?

If you sayNothing, I would act as I do
ThenA sound answer. If you do good because it is good, the account does not change your act. It changes what you expect after it.
If you sayI would hope more
ThenHope is what the verse offers. It does not ask you to hope into emptiness, but to hope with one who weighs fairly and gives generously.
If you sayI would pay more attention to small things
ThenThat is close to the heart of karma: the small is not lost. The verse adds that good is multiplied when the account is kept by someone generous.

The same in the other books

Translation

Also to you, Lord, belongs loving kindness, for you reward every man according to his work.

Original · Hebrew

וּלְךָֽ־אֲדֹנָ֥י חָ֑סֶד כִּֽי־אַתָּ֨ה תְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לְאִ֣ישׁ כְּֽמַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ׃

the Psalms · 62:12

World English Bible

Translation

If you say, “Behold, we didn’t know this,” doesn’t he who weighs the hearts consider it? He who keeps your soul, doesn’t he know it? Shall he not give to every man according to his work?

Original · Hebrew

כִּֽי־תֹאמַ֗ר הֵן֮ לֹא־יָדַ֪עְנ֫וּ זֶ֥ה הֲֽלֹא־תֹ֘כֵ֤ן לִבּ֨וֹת ׀ הֽוּא־יָבִ֗ין וְנֹצֵ֣ר נַ֭פְשְׁךָ ה֣וּא יֵדָ֑ע וְהֵשִׁ֖יב לְאָדָ֣ם כְּפָעֳלֽוֹ׃

Proverbs · 24:12

World English Bible

Let no man think lightly of evil, saying in his heart, It will not come nigh unto me. Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled; the fool becomes full of evil, even if he gather it little by little. Let no man think lightly of good, saying in his heart, It will not come nigh unto me. Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled; the wise man becomes full of good, even if he gather it little by little.

Buddhist texts · Dhp 121-122

Max Müller, 1881

Translation

The Rock: his work is perfect, for all his ways are just. A God of faithfulness who does no wrong, just and right is he.

Original · Hebrew

הַצּוּר֙ תָּמִ֣ים פָּעֳל֔וֹ כִּ֥י כָל־דְּרָכָ֖יו מִשְׁפָּ֑ט אֵ֤ל אֱמוּנָה֙ וְאֵ֣ין עָ֔וֶל צַדִּ֥יק וְיָשָׁ֖ר הֽוּא׃

the Torah (Deuteronomy) · 32:4

World English Bible
